name: School Counselor
description: ⚠⚠⚠ A Florida school counsellor carries 432 students. ASCA recommends 250 and the national average is 376 — so Florida runs 56 above the country and 182 above the standard. ⚠⚠ The credential is a Department of EDUCATION certification, not a Department of Health licence, which is the distinction that separates this from mental health counselling even though both mostly come out of the same master's code. ⚠ $64,330 median, 31,000 openings a year.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ TWO AGENCIES, TWO CREDENTIALS, ONE MASTER'S CODE — AND YOU MUST KNOW WHICH ONE YOUR PROGRAMME LEADS TO. School counselling in Florida is a CERTIFICATION issued by the Department of Education under Rule 6A-4.0181, F.A.C., Specialization Requirements for Certification in School Counseling (Grades PK-12). Mental health counselling is a LICENCE issued through the Department of Health under chapter 491. ⚠⚠ Both are normally taken inside a counselor education master's, and 285 of Florida's roughly 372 counselling master's seats sit under that single CIP code — so the same department, and sometimes the same building, produces graduates headed for two different regulators with different requirements. ⚠ Ask your programme directly which credential its track prepares you for, and whether a dual track exists. ⚠⚠⚠ THE RULE PRICES PRIOR TEACHING IN HOURS. Plan One requires a master's or higher with a graduate major in guidance and counseling or school counseling including a minimum of 600 CLOCK HOURS of supervised internship serving school-aged students in a prekindergarten, elementary or secondary setting. ⚠⚠ Plan Three cuts that to 300 CLOCK HOURS for a current full-time teacher employed at least 5 school years with effective or highly effective performance ratings in the most recent 3. Plan Two instead requires the employing district to attest that a certified school counsellor will mentor the applicant for the first two years of employment. ⚠ The rule is the authority and it was last amended effective 21 December 2025 — read the current text at flrules.org rather than relying on a summary, including this one.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ 432 students each

Students per school counsellor, 2023–24
✅ ASCA recommendation250
United States376
⚠⚠ Florida⚠⚠⚠ 432

Florida employs 6,649 school counsellors for 2,872,335 students. That is 56 more students per counsellor than the national average and 182 more than the standard ASCA has recommended since 1965.

⚠ For comparison in the same dataset: Hawaii 249, Colorado 253, Delaware 307, Connecticut 320. The national figure improved to 372:1 in 2024–25, its lowest since ASCA began tracking in 1986.

⚠⚠ Read this as the job description rather than as a grievance. A caseload of 432 decides what the work actually is: it is scheduling, testing, crisis response and triage far more than it is counselling, and anyone entering expecting sustained individual work should know that before the master's, not after.

⚠⚠⚠ Certification, not licensure — and they are different agencies

School counsellorMental health counselor
Credential✅ CERTIFICATION✅ LICENCE
Issued byDepartment of EducationDepartment of Health, chapter 491
AuthorityRule 6A-4.0181, F.A.C.s. 491.005(4), F.S.
Degreemaster's with a graduate major in school counseling⚠ CACREP master's of at least 60 semester hours
Supervised hours600 clock hours internship (300 for experienced teachers)700 hours practicum, 280 direct client services
After the degreedistrict mentoring under Plan Two⚠⚠ 2 years post-master's supervised practice

⚠⚠⚠ Both credentials mostly come out of the same place. 285 of Florida's roughly 372 counselling master's seats are coded counselor education — one CIP code, two regulators. The programme you enrol in has a track, and the track decides which of these two you end up eligible for.

⚠ So ask the question directly, before you enrol: does this track lead to DOE certification, to chapter 491 licensure, or to both? Programmes that prepare for both exist and are worth finding, because holding the LMHC alongside school certification opens private practice and summer work that the certification alone does not.

⚠⚠ Five years of teaching is worth 300 internship hours

RouteSupervised internship
Plan One — master's with a graduate major in school counseling600 clock hours
✅ Plan Three — current full-time teacher, 5+ years, effective or highly effective for the last 3⚠⚠ 300 clock hours
Plan Two — district attests a certified school counsellor will mentor you for 2 yearsmentoring route

⚠⚠⚠ This is the third Florida rule on this site that puts a number on a prior credential — alongside s. 468.1695 halving a nursing home administrator's training programme from 2,000 hours to 1,000 for a health administration major, and a CSWE-accredited BSW cutting Florida State's MSW from 61 credit hours to 39. Florida pays for relevant prior preparation in hours, in writing, and almost nobody tells students to look for it.

⚠ For a teacher considering the move, that is the single most useful fact here — the internship is the hardest part of a master's to fit around a full-time job, and five years in a classroom halves it.

The occupation

Educational, guidance and career counselors and advisors (21-1012)
2025 median$64,330
Employed (2024)376,300
Annual openings31,000
Growth 2024–34⚠ average (3% to 4%)

⚠⚠ Read the occupation title carefully: it is not only school counsellors. This SOC code also contains college academic advisers and career counsellors, so the 376,300 is a wider population than K-12 school counselling. Treat the wage as indicative and check your district's salary schedule, which is the number that will actually apply to you.

⚠ And note the growth rate against the neighbour. School and career counselling grows at 3–4%; mental health counselling grows at 18% with 50,500 annual openings. School counselling pays about $4,980 more and is expanding at roughly a fifth the rate.

⚠ Where the degree is, and one naming point

InstitutionCounselor education credentials (2023)
University of Central Florida69 master's + 18 postbaccalaureate certificates
Florida State University54 master's + 49 post-master's certificates
Florida Atlantic University50 master's + 11 post-master's certificates
Florida International University41 master's
Florida Gulf Coast University29 master's
University of South Florida16 master's
University of North Florida14 master's
University of Florida12 master's

⚠ Note the post-master's certificates — 60 of them across FSU and FAU. They are how somebody who already holds a counselling or education master's adds the school counselling specialisation, and they are the shortest route in for a career changer who is already qualified in something adjacent.

⚠⚠ One naming point worth knowing: the certification rule is now titled School Counseling. It used to be Guidance and Counseling, and both phrasings still appear across catalogues, job advertisements and district documents. They are the same certification — search for both.

Necessary skills

  • Triage. With 432 students, deciding who needs you this week is the core professional judgement.
  • Crisis intervention, which O*NET lists as a primary task and which arrives without notice.
  • Scheduling and graduation-requirement literacy — unglamorous, constant, and the thing that most affects a student's actual outcome.
  • Assessment interpretation: test data, records and interviews, turned into advice a sixteen-year-old will act on.
  • Working with parents, teachers and administrators who each want a different answer.
  • Mandatory reporting and record-keeping to a legal standard, because school records are disclosable and your notes are part of them.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Ask which credential the track leads to before you enrol. Department of Education certification and chapter 491 licensure are different regulators with different requirements, and both are taught inside counselor education programmes. A programme that prepares you for both is worth choosing.

⚠⚠ If you are already a teacher with five years and good evaluations, use Plan Three. It halves the internship from 600 clock hours to 300, and the internship is the part hardest to fit around a job.

⚠ If you already hold an adjacent master's, look at the post-master's certificate route. FSU and FAU awarded 60 of those in a single year; it is the shortest way in for a career changer.

⚠⚠ Go in knowing the caseload. 432 students is the Florida reality and it defines the job. Ask at interview how many students the post carries, how many counsellors the school has, and what share of the role is testing coordination — the answers vary enormously by district and they matter more than the salary.

And read the rule itself. 6A-4.0181 was amended effective 21 December 2025; certification rules change more often than degree requirements do, and the version that applies to you is the one in force when you apply.

programs.note: The degree — 8 Florida public institutions, 285 master's a year plus 60 post-master's and 18 postbaccalaureate certificates. ⚠⚠ The same code produces both school counsellors and mental health counsellors, so the TRACK inside the programme is what decides which credential you can apply for.

⚠⚠⚠ Not a prerequisite, but Rule 6A-4.0181 pays for it: a current full-time teacher with 5+ years and effective or highly effective ratings in the last 3 needs 300 internship clock hours instead of 600. ⚠ For a teacher considering the move, that halves the hardest part of the master's.

⚠ The commonest undergraduate feeder, and the caution is the same as on the mental health counselling page: Florida awards 6,228 psychology bachelor's a year against roughly 372 counselling master's seats. ⚠⚠ The bachelor's qualifies you for nothing here — the certification requires the master's.

⚠⚠ A real alternative inside schools: districts employ school social workers alongside counsellors, under a different certification and a different degree. ⚠ Florida awards 1,164 MSW a year against counselling's 372, so it is the better-resourced route into school-based work if the clinical side is what draws you.
⚠ Named because school-based mental health, prevention programming and youth risk behaviour work sit between the two fields, and district and county programmes employ both.

courses.reason: ⚠ Introduction to School Counseling — 6 institutions (FAMU, FAU, FSU, UCF, UF, UNF), the entry course of the school counselling track and the clearest signal that a programme runs one.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ GRADUATE. There is no undergraduate route to this certification — the MHS prefix is carried by 9 Florida universities and exactly one state college.

courses.reason: Internship in School Counseling — 3 institutions. ⚠ This is where Rule 6A-4.0181's 600 clock hours (or 300 under Plan Three) are actually served, in a PK-12 setting.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Confirm the placement setting counts: the rule requires supervised internship serving school-aged students in a prekindergarten, elementary or secondary school.

courses.reason: Supervised Field Experiences I — 5 institutions (FAMU, FAU, FIU, UNF, USF). The practicum that precedes the internship in most school counselling tracks.
Counseling Children and Adolescents — 5 institutions. The developmental and therapeutic core of school practice.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also numbered SDS6411 at FIU, UCF, UF and USF under the student development prefix. Register by number.

courses.reason: ⚠ Trauma and Crisis Counseling — 6 institutions. Crisis intervention is one of O*NET's primary tasks for this role and the part of the job that cannot be scheduled.
Career Development — 4 institutions. Career and lifestyle assessment is a named content area in the ch. 491 statute and it is a large share of what a school counsellor actually does.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried at undergraduate level as SDS3340 Career and Lifespan Development at FAU, FSU and UF — useful preparation, but not a substitute for the graduate course.

courses.reason: Measurement and Appraisal in Counseling — 4 institutions. Test interpretation, which O*NET lists as a core task and which school counsellors do constantly.
Multicultural Counseling and Development — 4 institutions. Social and cultural foundations is a required content area for the ch. 491 route and standard practice for the DOE one.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also numbered MHS6428 Counseling Diverse Populations at FGCU, FIU, UF and UNF.

courses.reason: Introduction to Family Counseling — 6 institutions. School problems are usually family problems, and this is where that is taught.
Addictions Counseling — 8 institutions, the most widely carried counselling course in Florida. ⚠ Relevant in schools as well as clinics, and a required content area for anyone also pursuing the LMHC.
Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. The undergraduate entry point, available at nearly every Florida state college.
Human Growth and Development — 29 institutions. Directly relevant, and a named content area for the licensure route if you pursue both credentials.

Introduction to the Teaching Profession — the education foundations entry course. ⚠ Named because the teaching route is what Plan Three rewards, and because school counsellors work inside a system a non-teacher has to learn from scratch.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers introductory education courses several ways (EDF2005, EDF1005, EDG2701). Check your catalogue.

courses.reason: Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Required for graduate admission, and school counselling increasingly involves reporting on outcomes and programme data.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. School records are disclosable documents and your notes are part of them.

Source data is NCES Common Core of Data 2023-24.

sources.note: The national student-to-school-counselor ratio was 372:1 in 2024–2025 against 376:1 the previous year, a 1% improvement and the lowest margin since ASCA began tracking ratios in 1986. ⚠ Only Colorado, Hawaii, New Hampshire and Vermont reported ratios within the 250:1 recommendation.

Plan Two substitutes two years of district mentoring. ⚠ Amended effective 21 December 2025.
